46	left and the group's **one derived sentence** in the lane, in secondary ink, nothing else.
47	
48	## The four groups, and their ranking
49	
50	| Group | Rows are | Ranked within by |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| **Now — waiting for you** | every open PR, each a bar from *opened* to *now*, wired to the item it ends or the issue it closes | age of the oldest PR in the row, oldest first; a row whose merge releases an edge sorts above one that releases nothing |
53	| **Flows — blocked, parked, waiting** | ad-hoc items and the plain issues that block them, placed at their **predicted run time** | broken lanes first (a blocker nothing is scheduled to move), then parks by park age, then sleepers by wake date |
54	| **Scheduled — the daily anchor** | a **task × day grid**: one row per daily task, then `weekly · N tasks` as one row | declaration order; the weekly row last |
55	| **Quiet** | one ruled line, not a row: the plain issues on no edge, counted by what matters (rotting, quick-win, needs-decision) | — |
56	
57	Now's header sentence is the **tomorrow-workload line** (below). Flows' header says how its
58	rows are placed. Scheduled's header names the anchor.
59	
60	### Collapse rules
61	
62	- PRs from one task under one landing policy collapse into a **thick bar** with a count
63	  (`9 PRs · 14 d → 2 d · policy: nothing`), its left end at the oldest and a `◂` where that
64	  is past the edge.
65	- Repeated verification items collapse into **one row of stacked park marks**, with the
66	  unpicked ones as a `◂` note.
67	- A ladder of plain issues (a migration plan's phases with `Blocked-by` and no queue mark)
68	  collapses into one gutter note, since none of it has a time.
69	- Each group is **capped at its worst four rows**, followed by one `N more rows` line naming
70	  what it holds; the list drops open on click, as HTML below the board.
71	- A plain issue reaches the board only where it sits on an edge; the rest are the quiet line.
72	
73	## Marks — what each is read from
74	
75	| Thing | Mark and place | Read from |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| open PR | a bar from `created_at` to *now* in the machine's blue; its length is its age; `◂` past the left edge | PR listing |
78	| PR waiting for a person | `▲` in amber above the bar's *now* end | no `Merge:` line on the item, or the task's `automerge` is `nothing`, or no work item names the PR at all; the run's own converge verdict lives in a comment the board does not fetch, so a PR whose item *does* authorize a merge reads as still open rather than as waiting |
79	| ad-hoc item, blocked on a date | hollow circle at its `Not-before` | body line, absolute form only |
80	| ad-hoc item, blocked on an issue | hollow circle **after** the blocker's predicted time; a PR blocker puts it at *now* + "when you merge"; a plain-issue blocker nothing is scheduled to close gives it **no time — the lane is drawn broken** | `Blocked-by: #n` and the blocker's own placement |
81	| ad-hoc item, ready | hollow circle at the next scheduler tick — the daily anchor, or the drain tick (its hour not read here) | `task:status:waiting-for-executor` |

86	| a relative date | flagged (`on a relative date`) in the `▸` note, never guessed | a `Not-before` in a form the parser does not read |

59	| **Fold age** | age of the *oldest* member's `usage.generated`; how many fold at all (`9 of 12 fold`) | `now − usage.generated`, max over folding members | fold stamp, read at head sha | oldest > 6 h on a member whose head moved → warning; a member that moved and has no fold → named |

input.title: `humanSeconds` has read 0 every day since it shipped — a human turn's gap lands on an `attachment` entry
input.body:
Found by the week-in-production retrospective of the dashboard redesign (#1624), reading `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` at `main`.

## The record

`humanSeconds` carries a key on all 29 day rows that have one, and its value is `0` on 28 of them (`1` on 2026-08-12). Over the same 29 days those rows count **843 user messages** and `agentSeconds` accumulates normally.

| day | sessions | userMessages | humanSeconds | agentSeconds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-03 | 7 | 35 | **0** | 9,266 |
| 2026-09-06 | 41 | 90 | **0** | 43,508 |
| 2026-09-07 | 13 | 21 | **0** | 11,521 |

## The cause

`turnSeconds` (`packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/fold-usage.mjs:516`) bills a turn's span as *previous stamped entry → this entry*, and adds it to `human` only when the entry passes `isUserMessage` (`:531`). In a real transcript the entry immediately before a human `user` entry is an `attachment` — written at the same millisecond the person sends — so the person's think-and-type gap ends on that `attachment`, which is neither a human message nor an `assistant` entry and is therefore dropped.

From `conversation-logs`, `2026-09-06T0631Z--issue-1746`:

```
attachment       06:06:50.183   gap 318.4 s   ← the person's think time, billed to nobody
queue-operation  06:09:18.160   gap 148.0 s
attachment       06:09:18.278   gap   0.031 s
user origin=human 06:09:18.281  gap   0.003 s ← the only gap billed as human
```

Across 8 captures from 2026-09-03 … 2026-09-08: **12 human turns, 0 human seconds, 5,902 agent seconds**. The entry immediately before a human turn was `attachment` 11 times and `queue-operation` once — never the assistant's last entry.

## The second defect in the same place

The fold writes `0` rather than leaving the key off. `foldDays` (`:741`) skips the two scalars only when `seconds` is `null`, and `turnSeconds` returns `{human: 0, agent: N}` whenever any entry is stamped. So a broken extraction is indistinguishable from a day nobody typed on — against this file's own rule (*no key where the source could not answer*) and against the repo rule that unknown is a state of its own, never a zero.

## What a fix has to do

- Bill a human turn's span from the last entry that is not harness bookkeeping (`attachment`, `queue-operation`, `atis-latch`, `last-prompt`, `mode`) up to the human entry, rather than from the immediately preceding stamped entry.
- Keep `humanSeconds` absent when no human turn on the day had a measurable predecessor, so a future regression reads as unknown rather than as zero.
- Pin it with a fixture carrying the real `attachment`-then-`user` shape; the current fixtures do not, which is why the suite stayed green through a week of zeroes.

The day rows already written are re-derivable: `foldDays` is stateless over the capture files, so a counting-bug fix self-heals the visible window on its next run. The **week** rows are not — they freeze — so the weeks already folded keep the zero.

input.title: `taskCost` files 89% of sessions under `(unresolved)` — the `(none)` bucket is unreachable
input.body:
Found by the week-in-production retrospective of the dashboard redesign (#1624), reading `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` at `main`.

## The record

Over the last 7 day rows, **63 of 71 sessions** are filed under `(unresolved)`; 8 name a task. `(none)` has appeared on **1 of 30** day rows (2026-08-12).

| day | sessions | `(unresolved)` | named |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-04 | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| 2026-09-05 | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| 2026-09-06 | 41 | 36 | 5 |
| 2026-09-07 | 13 | 11 | 2 |
| 2026-09-08 | 4 | 3 | 1 |

## The cause

`taskCostKey` (`packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/fold-usage.mjs:577`) returns a named task when the capture attests a `claudinite-task-exec` record, and otherwise discriminates on `issue > 0`:

```js
return issue > 0 ? TASK_COST_UNRESOLVED : TASK_COST_NONE;
```

Every capture this repo writes is filed under an issue — `captures` equals `merges` on all 30 day rows — so `issue > 0` is always true and `(none)` is unreachable in practice.

The module's own comment (`:569-573`) says `(unresolved)` is *"a session that names an issue but attests no execution record, which is a gap in the record rather than a person at the keyboard, and must never be quietly filed as one."* The data does exactly the reverse: a person at the keyboard is quietly filed as a record gap.

## What it costs

The repo page's per-task expand — tokens-per-close beside the model each task runs on (`repo-ledger.mjs`) — describes 11% of the week's sessions. The other 89% renders as a single `(unresolved)` row that a reader has to know is mostly people, and the human-driven share the design wanted visible (`:569-570`) is not drawn anywhere.

## Fix direction

The discriminator has to be *did a task run*, not *is there an issue number*. The `claudinite-task-exec` record already read at `:578` is that signal; a session with no such record is a person, whatever issue its capture happens to be filed under. `(unresolved)` then means what the comment says it means — a task session whose execution record did not reach the capture — and stays worth watching.

input.title: The Work board draws a row per PR and a row per item, not a lane per flow — `componentsOf` has no caller
input.body:
Found by the week-in-production retrospective of the dashboard redesign (#1624).

## What the design says

`packs/claudinite-dashboard/docs/work-board.md:29-33`:

> **The lane is the flow**, never the task and never the kind. […] A lane per kind (all PRs, all items, all issues) puts the two ends of one `Blocked-by` edge in different rows, and the edge is the whole point. So a row is one connected component of the edge graph […]

`board.mjs:14-17` repeats it in the module header.

## What the code does

`buildBoard` builds `nowRows` one per PR (`board.mjs:333`) and `flowRows` one per item (`:359`) — lanes by kind, the rejected design. `edgesOf` runs at `:330`, but its only consumer is `quietTail` (`:383`). `componentsOf` (`:98`) is exported and unit-tested and **has no caller outside its own test**.

The collapse rules are absent too (`work-board.md:60-71`): no thick bar per task-and-policy, no stacked park marks for repeated verifications, no ladder gutter note. So `GROUP_CAP = 4` has nothing to cap *down to* — it just hides rows.

## What that draws on this repo today

136 open issues, 7 open PRs, 51 queue items:

| group | rows | drawn |
|---|---|---|
| Now | 7 | 4 shown + `3 more rows` |
| **Flows** | **51** | **4 shown + `47 more rows`** |
| Quiet | 84 | one ruled line |

## The record says the component design was right

Computed over the live edge graph (58 item-and-PR nodes, 40 `Blocked-by` / `Ends-when` / `Closes` edges): **32 components**. 26 are singletons, but the 6 multi-node components hold **32 of the 58 nodes**:

- **14 nodes** — #1347, #1478, #1871–#1881, `pr:1890` (the claudinite-tasks reorganization ladder)
- **9 nodes** — #1640–#1643, #1909, `pr:1916`, `pr:1917`, `pr:1919`, `pr:1920` (the legacy-tolerance retirements)
- 3, 2, 2, 2 — the growth-promote pair and their PR, #1682/#1683, #1236/#1237, #1169/`pr:1513`

So the swimlanes-by-kind alternative the doc rejected is not vindicated by the record: the two longest chains are exactly the flows the board exists to make visible, and today they are 23 separate rows, 19 of them behind an `N more rows` line.

## One latent defect to fix with it

`edgesOf` keys PR nodes `pr:<n>` (`:91`) while `Ends-when: #<n>` pushes the bare number (`:88`). An item whose `Ends-when` names a pull request would therefore never join that PR's component even once `componentsOf` is wired up. Four open items are in exactly that shape today (#1640–#1643, each `Ends-when` a PR).

input.title: Decision: the fleet page's wake strip has read *not read* since it shipped — pay for the read or drop the cell
input.body:
A **design** finding from the week-in-production retrospective of the dashboard redesign (#1624) — the code does what the design says; the record shows the decision needs re-taking. Parked for the owner; nothing to implement until it is answered.

## The state

The *Next wake* cell on the fleet page's machine block reads *not read* on every render, and always will:

```js
// view-fleet.mjs:910
// The wake strip needs each task's own declared anchor, and a member read carries
// its task paths rather than their contents. So the strip is built from whatever
// rosters reached this page — none, today — and `machinePanel` states the absence
const rosterRows = resolved.flatMap((s) => (s.roster ?? []).map(...));
const strip = rosterRows.length ? wakeStrip(rosterRows, now) : null;
```

`resolved[].roster` is never populated by the fleet sweep, so `strip` is always `null` and `fleet-ledger.mjs:583` takes the `read: false` branch:

> `not read — N member(s) declare tasks, their anchors are in declarations this page does not fetch`

## Why this is a decision and not a bug

`docs/fleet-page.md:60` specifies the cell as derived from *"each member's declared tasks' `nextAsk.at` (`buildRoster`), collected fleet-wide"*, source *"task declarations at head sha"*, and gives it a **serious** bad-when. PR #1616 then declined that read at implementation time, on a stated ground: fetching the declarations is **one content request per member per task**, which is the one property the whole block is built not to spend — and an empty strip would read as *nothing wakes*, the serious verdict, so the absence has to say it is an absence.

Both halves are defensible. What the record adds is that the cautious choice has now stood for a full week with the cell giving nothing: a figure that reads *not recorded* every day for a week bought a row and gave nothing, which is the retrospective's own underuse test.

The doc was never corrected to match, so `fleet-page.md` still promises a read the page does not make and a bad-when it can never reach.

## The three ways out

1. **Pay the read.** One content request per member per task, behind the existing cache. Restores the cell the spec designed and the *unwired member* verdict that goes with it. Costs the property the block was built to protect.
2. **Move the anchor into what the fleet read already carries.** The sweep reads task *paths*; the anchor is in the declaration. A member could stamp its next anchors into an artifact the sweep already fetches (the fold, or the declaration stamp), making the strip one read for all of them. Largest change, cheapest steady state.
3. **Drop the cell.** The block loses the *is anything wired* question at fleet level; the repo page still answers it one member deep, where the roster is read.

Whichever is taken, `docs/fleet-page.md:60` needs correcting in the same change.

input.body:
Comment class: other

Retrospective run. #1602 merged as `256ddde` in #1616 at **2026-09-02T20:22:41Z**, read from the pull request, so the seven days are up and this is the ripe pass.

I read the five design documents first, then the record: `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` at `main` (`a31edea`, generated 2026-09-10T10:03Z), this repo's issues, pull requests and the fold's own closed work items, and eight captures on `conversation-logs` to attribute one figure's failure.

---

## The record against what was expected

**Five of the six new fold fields carry real values. One does not.**

| field | state |
|---|---|
| `tokensByModel` | ✅ every day with sessions, four models split apart |
| `prs` | ✅ **77 keys** across the last 7 day rows |
| `taskCost` | ⚠️ present, but **89% of sessions land in `(unresolved)`** — #1925 |
| `parks` | ✅ not zero: **21 parks** in the window (13 approval, 5 failure, 3 decision) |
| `ruleTokensByPack` | ✅ from 2026-09-03, the first fold after the merge — inside a day, as expected |
| `humanSeconds` / `agentSeconds` | ❌ `agentSeconds` works; **`humanSeconds` has read `0` on 28 of 29 days** — #1924 |

`prs` at 77 keys is well above the 15–30 predicted, and correctly so: the day rows count 56 merges on 2026-09-06 alone. The estimate was low, not the field.

**`usage-fold` kept closing `done`.** 7 runs over the 7 days, every one `outcome:done`, zero parks — the four new REST reads cost it nothing.

**The file grew 54,229 → 70,675 bytes over the week (+16.4 KB).** That is over the ~5 KB/week signal, but the stated cause is only a minority of it — see *Overuse* below.

---

## Is it working?

Mostly. The counters land, the fold stayed healthy, the pages have the data they were built on. Two of the six fields give materially less than the design promised, and the Work board's central structural argument was never wired up. Four findings, three of them actionable:

- **#1924** — `humanSeconds` reads 0 every day. `turnSeconds` bills a human turn's gap from the immediately preceding stamped entry, and the harness writes an `attachment` at the same millisecond the person sends, so the think-and-type gap is dropped. 843 user messages over 29 days produced **1 human second in total**. It also writes `0` rather than staying absent, so the breakage is indistinguishable from a quiet day.
- **#1925** — `taskCost`'s `(none)` bucket is unreachable (`issue > 0` is true for every capture, since `captures == merges` on all 30 day rows), so 63 of 71 sessions in the window read as a record gap. The per-task expand describes 11% of the week.
- **#1926** — the Work board draws a row per PR and a row per item. `componentsOf` is exported, unit-tested and has **no caller**; `edgesOf` feeds only the quiet tail. That is the lanes-by-kind design `work-board.md` explicitly rejects.
- **#1927** — *decision*, not a bug: the fleet page's wake strip.

## Is it misused?

No. The fold's new per-item events read did not become eager: `usage-fold` ran 7/7 clean with no rate-limit failures and no visible wall-time growth. The watermark bounds it adequately.

## Is it overused?

**Yes, on the board's cap — and the diagnosis in this issue's own signal was right.** Against this repo today (136 open issues, 7 open PRs, 51 queue items):

| group | rows | drawn |
|---|---|---|
| Now | 7 | 4 shown + `3 more rows` |
| **Flows** | **51** | **4 shown + `47 more rows`** |
| Quiet | 84 | one ruled line |

N = 47, far above ~15, permanently. And the reason is exactly the one predicted: the collapse rules (thick bar per task-and-policy, stacked park marks, ladder gutter note) are not implemented, so `GROUP_CAP = 4` has nothing to collapse *into* and simply hides 47 rows. Filed as #1926 with the lane defect, because they are one fault: a cap only works over rows that have already been collapsed by flow.

**No, on the week-tier `prs` key space** — the file's growth is real but the named cause is a minority of it:

| tier | contribution |
|---|---|
| frozen week rows | W35 `2,123 B` → W36 `7,123 B` = **+5.0 KB/week**, of which `prs` is **1,868 B** (89 keys) — the rest is `checkFindings` 1,755 B, `parks` 712 B, `taskCost` 368 B |
| day rows | +11 KB, but the day tier is a rolling 30-day window still backfilling with the six new fields; it stops around 2026-10-02 |

So `prs` costs ~1.9 KB a frozen week at this repo's merge rate, not the whole +16 KB. It is worth re-reading in a month against a steady-state file rather than acting on now. W36 was also this repo's heaviest week on record (56 merges in one day).

## Is it underused?

Three figures bought a row and gave little or nothing. Naming each with its fix:

1. **`humanSeconds` — reads 0 every day.** Fix is **extraction** (#1924). The source is there; the reader looks in the wrong place.
2. **`taskCost` `(none)` — never populated; `(unresolved)` holds 89%.** Fix is **extraction** (#1925). The join key is wrong, not missing.
3. **The fleet page's wake strip — always *not read*, by construction.** Fix is a **decision** (#1927): pay one content request per member per task, move the anchor into an artifact the sweep already reads, or delete the cell. The design doc still promises the read and a `serious` bad-when the cell can never reach, so `fleet-page.md:60` needs correcting whichever way it goes.

One more worth a note but not an issue: **`prs.sessionToMergeHours` is unknown on 59% of the week's PRs, and 28 of the 31 known values are exactly `0`** — three of 77 PRs carry a non-zero. That is a true fact (auto-merge is effectively instant) rather than a broken figure, but as a *sample* it is one constant repeated 28 times, which is an argument for the quantile the design deliberately rejected — for this field only. `leadHours` is complete (77/77) and `issueLeadHours` 73% known; both earn their place.

---

## The wrong-design signals

- **`work-board.md` rejected swimlanes by kind for connected components** — *the rejection was right*, and the record says so. Over the live graph (58 item-and-PR nodes, 40 edges) there are 32 components; 26 are singletons, but the 6 multi-node components hold **32 of the 58 nodes**, including a 14-node chain (#1347, #1478, #1871–#1881, PR #1890) and a 9-node chain (#1640–#1643, #1909 and their four PRs). Those two flows are 23 separate rows today, 19 of them hidden behind `N more rows`. Detail in #1926.
- **`repo-page.md`'s 450 px budget, shipped at 486** — **not re-measured.** This is a rendered-page measurement, and it is not one of the five reads this issue's record table names; re-running it needs the one-off harness PR #1616 built, which is not in the tree. I am not reporting it clean. One thing that has changed under it: `humanSeconds` now emits a number instead of a wrapped *not recorded* sentence, so one of the two lines the 486 px was spent on is gone — for the wrong reason, and it comes back when #1924 is fixed correctly.
- **`fleet-page.md` rejected a member × signal matrix for 12 heartbeat squares** — **not judged.** It needs the fleet page rendered against fleet data, which no read in this repository provides: this session carries no member scope and the fold here is one member's. Not a blocked read from the record table — an evidence source the record table never claimed.

---

## Two housekeeping notes

- **#1609 is this same retrospective**, parked `needs-human-decision`; #1884 already tracks the missing dedup guard that let both be filed. Nothing here duplicates work done there — #1609 was never run — but the pair should converge together.
- This run opened **no pull request**. Its request issue prescribes issues and this summary as the deliverable (step 3); an implementation fault is an actionable task issue, not a fix slipped into a retrospective run.
